title: Measures of Central Tendency
summary: Mean, median and mode are single values that represent the centre of a set of data. Range, class mark and frequency are not measures of central tendency.

Raw data: mean x̄ = (sum of observations)/(number of observations). The first five primes 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 have mean 28/5 = 5.6; the first five multiples of 7 have mean 105/5 = 21. If each observation is increased by k, the mean increases by k. A wrongly copied value is corrected by fixing the total: 9 observations with mean 35 total 315; reading 81 as 18 lost 63, so the true mean is 378/9 = 42.

Ungrouped (discrete) frequency data: x̄ = Σfᵢxᵢ/Σfᵢ. Grouped data: take each class mark (midpoint) as xᵢ and use the same formula (direct method). Assumed mean method: x̄ = a + Σfᵢdᵢ/N with dᵢ = xᵢ − a; step deviation: x̄ = a + (Σfᵢuᵢ/N) × h with uᵢ = (xᵢ − a)/h. To find a missing frequency or value p, write Σfx and Σf in terms of p, set Σfx = x̄ × Σf, and solve.

Arrange the data in order. If n is odd, the median is the ((n + 1)/2)th value; if n is even, it is the mean of the (n/2)th and (n/2 + 1)th values. The median of 10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20 is (14 + 16)/2 = 15. For a frequency table, make the cumulative frequency (cf) column and find the value whose cf first reaches the required position. For grouped data (asked in some papers), the median class is the one whose cf first reaches N/2, and median = l + ((N/2 − cf)/f) × h, where l is its lower limit, cf the cumulative frequency before it, f its frequency and h the class size.

The mode is the value that occurs most often (the one with the highest frequency). For 2, 7, 5, 9, 5, 7, 8, 11, 5 the mode is 5. Empirical relation for moderately skewed data: mode = 3 median − 2 mean (mean 27, mode 45 ⇒ median 33).
mcq: The mean of the first five prime numbers is —

mcq.work: There are 6 values (even), so take the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (14 + 16)/2 = 15.

mcq: The mean of the first five multiples of 7 is —

mcq.work: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35: sum = 105; mean = 105/5 = 21. (For an A.P. of odd length, the mean is the middle term.)

mcq: The mean of 5 observations is 15. The mean of the first three is 14 and of the last three is 17. The third observation is —

mcq.work:
Total = 5 × 15 = 75. First three = 42; last three = 51.
42 + 51 counts the third observation twice: 93 − 75 = 18.

mcq: If the mean of 6, 7, p, 8, q, 14 is 9, then —
The middle-most observation of ordered data is the —

mcq.work: By definition the median is the middle value of data arranged in order.

mcq: Which of the following is NOT a measure of central tendency?

mcq.work: Mean, median and mode describe the centre. Range (highest − lowest) measures spread. (April 2024 asked the same with 'class mark'.)
5 occurs three times, 7 twice, others once. Mode = 5.

mcq: If the mean of x₁, x₂, …, x₁₀ is 20, the mean of x₁ + 4, x₂ + 4, …, x₁₀ + 4 is —

mcq.work: Adding 4 to every value adds 4 to the mean: 20 + 4 = 24.

mcq: If the mean of grouped data is 27 and the mode is 45, the median is —
objective: Fill in the blanks: (i) If the mode of 12, 16, 19, 16, x, 12, 16, 19, 12 is 16, then x = ____. (ii) If the median of a data is 24 and each item is increased by 2, the new median is ____.

(i) 12 occurs 3 times and 16 three times; for 16 to be the only mode it must occur more, so x = 16.
(ii) Adding 2 to every item adds 2 to the median: 26.
Write True or False: (i) Class mark is a measure of central tendency. (ii) The median of 3, 1, 5, 2, 4 is 5.

(i) False: mean, median and mode are; a class mark is just a class's midpoint.
(ii) False: in order 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 the middle value is 3.
Fill in the blanks: (i) Two measures of central tendency are ____ and ____. (ii) The mean of 9 observations is 35; if 81 was misread as 18, the correct mean is ____.

(i) mean and median (also mode).
(ii) Wrong total = 315; correct total = 315 − 18 + 81 = 378; mean = 378/9 = 42.

items: The cumulative frequency up to 55 kg is —

vsa:
N = 61 (odd) ⇒ median = 31st value.
cf: 5, 16, 40, 56, 61. The 31st value lies where cf first reaches 31 — at x = 35.
Median = 35.

N = 80 (even) ⇒ mean of the 40th and 41st values.
cf: 8, 18, 34, 58, 73, 80. Both the 40th and 41st lie in x = 35.
Median = 35.

N = 70 ⇒ 35th and 36th values.
cf: 3, 10, 22, 42, 70. Both lie at x = 20. Median = 20.
The mean of 9 observations is 35. If 81 was wrongly copied as 18, find the correct mean.

Wrong total = 9 × 35 = 315. Correct total = 315 − 18 + 81 = 378.
Correct mean = 378/9 = 42.

N = 25 ⇒ 13th value. cf: 4, 10, 17, 20, 25.
The 13th lies at x = 15. Median = 15.
If the mean of the data is 15, find p: x: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25; f: 6, p, 6, 10, 5.
The data 11, 12, 14, 18, x + 2, x + 4, 30, 32, 35, 41 is in ascending order and its median is 24. Find x.

n = 10 ⇒ median = mean of 5th and 6th = ((x + 2) + (x + 4))/2 = x + 3.
x + 3 = 24 ⇒ x = 21.
The data 50, 42, 35, 2x + 10, 2x, 18, 12, 11 is in descending order and its median is 25. Find x.

n = 8 ⇒ median = mean of 4th and 5th = (2x + 10 + 2x)/2 = 2x + 5.
2x + 5 = 25 ⇒ x = 10.
N = 33 ⇒ 17th value. cf: 2, 5, 10, 14, 21, … The 17th lies at x = 39. Median = 39.
sa: If the mean of the data is 6, find P: x: 2, 4, 6, 10, P + 5; f: 3, 2, 3, 1, 2.
The mean of the distribution is 35 and Σf = 25. Find x₁ and x₂: classes 0–10, 10–20, …, 60–70; f: 1, x₁, 5, 7, x₂, 3, 1.
la: An insurance company recorded the ages at death: 0–10: 2, 10–20: 12, 20–30: 55, 30–40: 95, 40–50: 71, 50–60: 42, 60–70: 16, 70–80: 7. Find the mean age.

N = 155 ⇒ median is the 78th value.
cf: 3, 10, 22, 42, 70, 101, 129, 155. The 78th lies at x = 30. Median = 30.
The highest frequency is 31, at x = 30. Mode = 30.
